title: Theorem E (cusp degeneration + Schwartz-Zippel): mindeg(N)=N-1 off a fraction w_N/p, w_N ~ N^4/3
question: Is the cusp-degeneration bound (agent label "Theorem D" in RUN-04709f64; renamed Theorem E to avoid collision with the Hasse side-condition Theorem D) correct as stated verbatim below?
rationale: Proof attempt from ECDLP-38 giving deficit 0 generically for N < p^{1/4}; partial progress on conjecture C*.
assumptions: Standard division-polynomial identities D1 (numerically checked, not re-proved)
Schwartz-Zippel lemma (standard; agent cited it from recollection)
claims:
VERBATIM from RUN-04709f64 report: **Theorem D (proof attempt, complete modulo the standard facts in D1).** Let p be prime, N >= 3, p > 2N, and set w_N := (N-1)[ N(N+1)(2N+1)/6 - (N+2)/2 ] = N^4/3 + O(N^3). Let Z = {tau in F_p^3 : curve nonsingular, kP != O and x_1..x_N distinct (i.e. (i+-l)P != O, 1<=l<i<=N) , c_{N-1} = 0}. Then
 (a) target k^2: |Z| <= w_N p^2 (fraction <= w_N/p of the p^3 triples (A, x0, y0)), for every such p;
 (b) target k: the same bound whenever p not in Bad_N.
Hence for such p, all but a fraction w_N/p of (curve, point) pairs have mindeg(N) = N-1 exactly (deficit 0) [by L1]; deficits D >= D0 >= 1 are a subset.
Proof. On U = {prod_{m<=2N-1} psi_m(tau) != 0}, write c_{N-1} = sum_i f_i prod_{l != i}(x_i-x_l)^{-1}. By D1, 1/prod_{l!=i}(x_i-x_l) = prod_{l!=i} (-theta_i theta_l/(psi_{i+l}psi_{i-l})) with theta = psi^2 (signs by ordering). Multiply by W = prod_{a<b} psi_{a+b}psi_{b-a}: c_{N-1} = Num/W with Num = sum_i +-f_i theta_i^{N-1} prod_{l!=i}theta_l * prod_{a<b; a,b != i} psi_{a+b}psi_{b-a} a polynomial in (A,B,x0,y0). A weight count shows every summand has the same weight 2(N-1)S2 - (N-1)(N+2), S2 = sum l^2 (independent of i; hand-derived, w_N equals half of it; N=2 gives 6 = wt(psi_2^2), consistent with c_1 = -psi_2^2/psi_3). Substituting B = y0^2-x0^3-A x0 keeps weight, and every variable has weight >= 2, so deg Num <= w_N. At tau0 = (0,1,1): psi_m(tau0) = m != 0 for m < p, so tau0 in U, x_k(tau0) = 1/k^2, and (Num/W)(tau0) = cusp divided difference of D0, nonzero under (a) or (b)'s hypotheses. So Num is a nonzero polynomial of degree <= w_N, and Z is contained in its zero set; Schwartz-Zippel (unverified recollection of the standard lemma) gives |Z| <= w_N p^2. QED.

**Corollary D' (characteristic 0, generic).** Over Q(A,x0,y0) (and hence on a Zariski-open dense set of (A,B,P) over any field of characteristic 0 / in the cusp's neighbourhood), c_j != 0 for every j >= 0 and both targets, i.e. mindeg(N) = N-1 for every N. Proof: D0 (i),(ii) give nonvanishing at tau0, and the same specialisation argument. Numerically illustrated (check A: c_j(eps)/c_j(0) -> 1 as eps -> 0 on rational curves).

**Obstruction / sharpness remarks.** (1) The qualifier "generic" cannot be dropped: L3 (proved) gives deficit >= 1 on anomalous j=0 curves, and in char 0 the hypersurface c_2 = 0 (x1+x3 = 2x2) meets real curves (check D: sign change at A in (1.6,1.7), P=(1,1), B=-A) so there is no all-curves statement of this type. (2) The bound w_N/p is non-trivial only for N <~ (3p)^{1/4}; the true deficit frequency is ~1/p (check E), so the method loses a factor N^4. It improves alpha from 1/3 to 1 only for N <~ p^{1/4}, and only generically; for large N it gives no improvement on Theorem C. (3) For N > p^{1/4} the structure c_{N-1} = Num/W with deg Num ~N^4 means no argument via a single specialisation can reach N ~ p; a different input (e.g. sharper degree of the irreducible factors of Num, or Lang-Weil/Chebotarev on the hypersurface Num = 0 showing it is geometrically irreducible with ~p^2 points) would be needed.

## Numerical checks (all in research/ecdlp/experiments/round11-cstar/, stdlib, seeded or deterministic, total < 2 min)
- A. cusp.py -> out_cusp.txt: exact Fractions, n <= 16: all c_j(0) != 0 with sign (-1)^j (target k); target k^2 c_j = (-1)^j (j+1)!^2 (first 6 confirmed); the hypothesis "numerators are (2j+1)-smooth" was FALSE for j >= 2 (negative result; leads to Bad_N). Rational lift: P=(1,1), A=3 eps, N=10: c_j(eps)/c_j(0) = 1.0000002510 (j=2), 1.0000945 (j=5), 1.0074 (j=9) at eps=1e-9; ratios -> 1 as eps -> 1e-18. At eps=1e-3 or 1e-6 the ratios are far from 1 for j=9 (the O(eps) coefficient grows quickly with N).
- B. cusp_modp.py -> out_cusp_modp.txt: all primes 5 <= p < 400, 3 <= N <= (p-1)/2: target k^2: c_j(0) != 0 mod p for all j<N (asserted, never failed); target k: c_{N-1}(0) = 0 mod p in 33 of 6751 pairs (0.49%, random model 0.52%); with N <= 12: (p,N) = (11,3),(19,6),(31,10),(151,4); none at N = (p-1)/2.
- C. divpoly_check.py -> out_divpoly.txt: 1080 assertions of identities for x_m and x_i - x_l on random curves mod 10007 (seed 11); psi_m(cusp) = m for m <= 20; table of w_N.
- D/E. exhaust.py -> out_exhaust.txt: exhaustive over all (A,x0,y0) in F_p^3, p = 31 and 43, N = 3..8, nodes distinct: fraction with c_{N-1} = 0 is 0.016-0.049 (p=31, 1/p=0.032) and 0.019-0.027 (p=43, 1/p=0.023), both targets; consistent with 1/p and far below the proved bound w_N/p (vacuous at these toy sizes, >1). Real-curve scan found a sign change of x1+x3-2x2.
Limitations of checks: toy primes; finite domain only; Theorem D's degree bound w_N is not tested for tightness.

## Literature
- Coppersmith-Shparlinski, J. Cryptology 13 (2000) 339-360: exponential-in-log p degree lower bounds for polynomials agreeing with the discrete logarithm on >= p^{1/2+eps} points (character sums); different regime (F_p^* DL on subsets, not x-only EC nodes with a fixed multiplier structure). Verified from abstracts via search, full text not read.
- Lange-Winterhof (COCOON 2002; AAECC 2003) and Kiltz-Winterhof (Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. 2004; Discrete Appl. Math. 154 (2006)): degree lower bounds for ECDH/ECDL interpolation; exact statements not read. A WCC 2005 abstract mentions improved ECDL bounds for curves with an endomorphism of degree 2 or 3 (author unverified).
- Kopparty-Kothary-Shankar, ePrint 2026/2621 (preprint, not checked): sharper Coppersmith-Shparlinski bound.
- Schwartz-Zippel lemma and standard division-polynomial identities: unverified recollection (identities checked numerically here).
No source gives the cuspidal-degeneration argument; I did not find it in the literature (absence of evidence only).
D0 (cusp divided differences): target k^2 gives f[y_1..y_{j+1}] = (-1)^j (j+1)!^2 x0^{-j} != 0.
